tool.name: sigma_rules_for_technique
tool.description:
Look up Sigma detection rules for a MITRE ATT&CK technique. First 🟡 important item from the §10 expert-pentester gap audit. Closes the loop on the #66 ATT&CK tagging — turns "this finding maps to T1190" into "this finding maps to T1190; here are 12 Sigma rules across Splunk / Elastic / Sentinel that detect attempts in your SIEM".
Sigma rules carry MITRE ATT&CK tags like `attack.t1190` / `attack.t1190.001` in their YAML `tags:` field. We use GitHub Code Search with `attack. repo:SigmaHQ/sigma extension:yml`.
**Display-only** — does NOT emit findings (LLM-output / corpus search; agent should treat as enrichment data). The agent integrates the rule list into existing findings via the report's `references` field or the wrapper's display layer. Same pattern as `exploit_refs` (#62).
Auth: `STRIX_GITHUB_TOKEN` is **required** (GitHub Code Search needs authentication). Without it, returns `success=False` with a clear error so the agent knows the data isn't available for this scan. `github_token` parameter overrides the env var.
Cache: per-(technique, max_results) JSON cache under `~/.strix/sigma_cache/`, 24-hour TTL. Stale-cache served on network failure (fail-open with `error` populated). Disable with `STRIX_SIGMA_NO_CACHE=1`.
MITRE technique: T1593.003 (Search Open Websites/Domains: Code Repositories) — surfaced via #66 ATT&CK tagging.
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies; `--exclude-path` doesn't apply (URL is api.github.com / SigmaHQ, not the customer's domain).

parameter.name: technique
parameter.description: ATT&CK technique ID (e.g. `T1190`, `T1190.001`). Case-insensitive on input; normalised to upper-case. Returns `success=False` for malformed input (anything not matching `T(.)?`).

parameter.name: max_results
parameter.description: Hard cap on rules returned. Default 20. GitHub Code Search per_page max is 100; values above 100 are clamped.

parameter.name: github_token
parameter.description: Optional override for the GitHub API token. Default reads from `STRIX_GITHUB_TOKEN` env. **Required** — GitHub Code Search needs authentication.

returns.description:
{success, technique, queried_at, from_cache, rules: [{name, path, html_url, url, sha, repo}, ...], rule_count, max_results, source_errors, error?}.
The agent should: 1. Surface the `rules[].html_url` list in finding descriptions / report references so the customer's SIEM team can deploy the rules directly. 2. Pair with `cve_lookup` (#61) and `exploit_refs` (#62) to give a full enrichment package per finding: "vulnerable component → public exploit → SIEM detection rule". 3. Note that the rules use SigmaHQ's YAML format; the customer's SIEM may need a Sigma → backend conversion (sigmac / pySigma) to consume them.
